text: They wanted to cancel their internet.
The employee wouldn't stop asking why.
July 2014. Veronica Belmont calls Comcast to disconnect.
She explains. He asks again. Ten minutes in, she hands the phone to her husband, Ryan Block.
"Why is it that you're not wanting to have the number one rated internet service?"
Ryan: "This phone call is actually an amazing representative example of why I don't want to stay with Comcast."
Eighteen minutes in all. Finally... disconnected.
Veronica still went to a Comcast store to double-check.
Ryan posted the recording. It went viral.
Comcast apologized. How the employee spoke was "not consistent with how we train."
Ryan asked them not to fire him.
A week later, an internal memo from Comcast's COO leaked.
The employee, it said, "did a lot of what we trained him and paid him... to do."
It added: keeping a customer must be done with respect.
One employee was on the line.
Behind him... the training. And the pay.
